Preston-Snoqualmie Trail.surface_summary: Paved with soft shoulder; 0.2 mi gravel switchbacks near SE 68th St / Preston-Fall City Rd.
Preston-Snoqualmie Trail.ebike: Class 1 and 2 allowed on King County regional trails, 15 mph limit (kc-rules). Conflict: the trail's own page says "No electric vehicles are allowed on the trail" (kc-pst), likely predating the 2024 rule change; obey any posted signs.

notes.text: Bridge #2 closed indefinitely since a December 2022 storm; no detour. The trail is split into two sections.
Steep, tight gravel switchbacks near the old Raging River trestle site (about 0.2 mi, not ADA accessible).
Crosses Preston-Fall City Rd SE: use the crossing flags and watch for traffic.
In fall, after leaf drop, the eastern end offers glimpses of Snoqualmie Falls.
Bridge #2 location: King County says about 0.75 mi east of the Preston-Snoqualmie Trailhead lot; OpenStreetMap places the closed trestle about 0.78 mi west of the Lake Alice lot.

access.name: Preston Athletic Fields and Community Park
High Point Way access
access.notes: Preston Park & Ride is nearby; it is a transit lot, check posted rules.

access.name: Lake Alice Trailhead
access.address: 5517 Lake Alice Rd SE, Fall City, WA

Snoqualmie Valley Trail.ebike: Class 1 and 2 allowed on King County regional trails, 15 mph limit (kc-rules).

notes.text: Reinig Bridge in Snoqualmie closed due to repeated vandalism; anticipated to reopen 12/31/2026.
Trail is interrupted around the Snoqualmie Mill site: stairs at Tokul Rd and at SE Reinig Rd, with a 2.5 mi on-street detour between. Shown here as two separate pieces.
Tokul Trestle; North Fork Snoqualmie River; farmland.

access.name: Stillwater Wildlife Area lot (WDFW)
access.notes: OSM tags this WDFW lot fee=yes with pass card payment; WDFW lands generally need a Discover Pass. Not confirmed with WDFW.

access.name: Rattlesnake Lake Recreation Area
access.notes: Dawn to dusk; parking free but limited, heavy weekend use (SPU).

Cedar River Trail.surface_summary: Paved for the first 12.3 mi from Lake Washington in Renton; soft surface for the last 5 mi to Landsburg.
Cedar River Trail.ebike: Class 1 and 2 allowed on King County regional trails, 15 mph limit (kc-rules).

notes.text: A portion near the Dorre Don Natural Area is closed due to winter 2025 flood damage; exact limits and reopening date not published.
Lake Washington and downtown Renton; Cedar River along its length.

access.name: Ron Regis Park (Renton)
access.notes: King County lists the park as accessible from the trail; parking lot located from OSM.

access.name: Landsburg Trailhead
access.notes: East end of the trail on Landsburg Rd SE.

East Lake Sammamish Trail.ebike: Class 1 and 2 allowed on King County regional trails, 15 mph limit (kc-rules, kc-elst).

notes.text: 600 ft closed between Louis Thompson Rd NE and NE Inglewood Hill Rd from June 1, 2026 through the end of 2026 (culvert replacement); no detour.
Waterfront trail along Lake Sammamish.

access.name: NE Inglewood Hill Rd parking area (Sammamish)
Sammamish Landing Park
access.notes: Named lot adjacent to the trail (OSM: 34 spaces, no fee).

Lake Sammamish State Park.surface_summary: Park path network; surfaces vary (see map flags).
Lake Sammamish State Park.ebike: State Parks e-bike rules not yet verified for this park; obey posted signs.

notes.text: Issaquah Creek and Tibbetts Creek bridges closed due to erosion; no repair timeline.
Homestead Trail closed until further notice due to a washout.
Bike access on the park's footpaths isn't confirmed; check posted signs.

access.name: Lake Sammamish State Park: Tibbetts Beach lot
access.notes: Beach lot by the playground (OSM: 250 spaces). Address shown is the park's address. Park hours 6:30 a.m. to dusk; restrooms and drinking water listed by State Parks.

access.name: Lake Sammamish State Park: Sunset Beach lot
access.notes: Large beach lot (OSM: 1,200 spaces, Discover Pass required). Address shown is the park's address. Park hours 6:30 a.m. to dusk.

Eastrail.surface_summary: Mixed paved and gravel sections; King County doesn't publish a section-by-section surface list, so per-section surface comes from OpenStreetMap.
Eastrail.ebike: Class 1 and 2 allowed on King County regional trails, 15 mph limit (kc-rules).

notes.text: Wilburton Trestle under construction since May 2024; anticipated opening mid-2027.
Central Wilburton segment (0.65 mi, NE 8th St bridge to the trestle) will open as an interim gravel trail, anticipated 2027.
The I-90 crossing is the final gap in the southern segment; anticipated opening 2031.

access.name: Newcastle Beach Park
access.address: 4400 Lake Washington Blvd SE, Bellevue, WA 98006
access.notes: City park lot about 200 m from Eastrail. Parking is limited and first-come; designated lots only (City of Bellevue). Restrooms and beach in the park.

Cross Kirkland Corridor.surface_summary: Ten-foot-wide crushed gravel interim trail, South Kirkland Park & Ride to Totem Lake; paving is planned in the master plan but not built.
Cross Kirkland Corridor.ebike: Electric-assisted bicycles allowed; 15 mph speed limit (kirkland-ckc).

notes.text: Closed between NE 52nd St and 108th Ave NE for King County culvert repair, starting as early as Sept. 8, 2026, for about three months; detour available.
Part of Eastrail.
